Export profiles are reusable bundles of filter rules: inclusions, exclusions, reference-only patterns, and the base toggles (binaries, gitignore, size limit). Built-in profiles cover common project types; save your own from the dialog once you have tuned a selection you like.\n\nSelecting a profile re-scans the tree with that profile\'s rules. Any manual adjustments you had made in the tree under a different profile are discarded on preset switch, because they belonged to the previous profile\'s context. They will reappear when you switch back to that profile.

When this section is enabled and the project is a Git repository, you can export a Git snapshot instead of the current working tree.

Pick a branch, tag, or commit using the search icon next to the ref field, or type any expression Git can resolve (HEAD~3, origin/main, v1.2.0). The resolved short hash appears under the field so you can confirm the target before generating.

Preview diff shows what would change between the selected ref and the working tree, without modifying anything. Useful to sanity-check what the export is going to contain.

You can disable Git entirely from the plugin settings page; the section will then show a "disabled globally" notice. .gitignore rules keep working either way.

Unchecking the Version control box disables the whole section without losing the configured reference: the ref stays in the profile and is reapplied the next time you check the box.

Tree v2: the project tree is now the authoritative source of what goes into the dump. Every entry can be Included, Reference-only, or Excluded directly from the tree, and the selection is preserved per project.

Reference-only entries: list a file in the dump by name and size without reading its content. Ideal for lockfiles, generated code, and machine-local configuration. Marked with a [ref] suffix in the tree header and a [content omitted: N B — reference only] marker in the body.

Uniform folder cycling: clicking a folder forces the next state onto every non-locked descendant at every depth, so the folder indicator never disagrees with its children. Marking a deep file updates every ancestor up to the root without touching its siblings.

Show locked: hard-excluded folders and binary files appear as locked nodes. Enabling the toggle makes them interactive and scans their contents on demand; disabling it re-locks everything and discards what was included while unlocked.

New General section: \"Exclude binary files\" and \"Maximum size\" now live under their own uppercase title at the top of the form, instead of floating unlabelled between the preset spinner and Inclusions.

Section toggles: Inclusions, Exclusions, Reference only, Gitignore, Version control, and File tree all follow the same checkbox + uppercase title + help pattern. Unchecking Inclusions, Exclusions, or Reference only disables the list without deleting it, and a Clear button next to Add empties the flow in one tap.

Dark theme is now the default. A fresh install opens on the plugin\'s original hand-tuned palette. The theme selector still offers System and Light, and existing users who explicitly picked a theme keep their stored choice.
Info screen redesigned: features grouped into four categories, per-row icon count cut from roughly 25 to 10, and a hero block with a version and status chip row.
Project root resolution: three-step heuristic (.gitignore search, CodeAssist project boundary, fallback to the selected folder), bounded by the new \"Parent folder search limit\" setting.

The plugin\'s own .platform directory is now hard-excluded from the dump, alongside .git, .gradle, and .idea, so the per-project config can never end up in the model\'s context. Contextual help is now available on every section.
Follow these steps to enable One Code For AI in your IDE.
Get the latest .apk from the official repository or the distribution channel.
Open the APK on your device and accept the install from unknown sources if prompted.
Once installed, launch the CodeAssist app on your device.
Go to Settings > Plugins > Installed and enable One Code For AI. It will load automatically.
Close and reopen CodeAssist so all components load correctly.
Export a project as AI-ready context in four steps.
Tap the project file tree in CodeAssist
The options context menu will open
The option to generate the dump will appear
Save the .txt to Download or send it to your AI

Find answers to common issues and learn how to get the most out of the plugin.
How do I disable Git functionality entirely?
Go to CodeAssist Settings, then Plugins, and open the One Code For AI settings. There you will find the \"Git integration\" toggle. When disabled, the plugin treats your folder as plain files.
Why does .gitignore still work when Git is disabled?

If Git is disabled, the plugin automatically searches your selected folder and its parent directories for a .gitignore file. The search is bounded by the \"Parent folder search limit\" setting, which defaults to 10 levels and can be raised from the settings page.
What do the amber .gitignore rules mean?

A rule is highlighted in amber when one of your manual inclusion, exclusion, or reference-only filters is actively overriding it. Inclusions, exclusions, and reference-only patterns always take priority over .gitignore.
How do I use glob patterns in filters?
Use standard glob syntax: *.log (any log file), build/ (specific folder), and double-star path globs for any nested generated folder. Tap the \"?\" icon next to the filter sections for a quick guide.
What do the new Android presets do?

Android (Kotlin) exports everything. Android (source only) strips tests and docs. Android (Resources) exports only XMLs (layouts/themes). Generated files like R.java and local.properties are listed as reference-only by default.
Where are the settings for animations and notifications?
They are in the native CodeAssist settings for this plugin. Disabling animations helps performance on low-end devices. Disabling notifications silences progress and completion alerts.
How do I exclude an entire folder easily?
Open the file tree preview in the configuration dialog. Click the folder\'s tri-state indicator until it cycles to the excluded state. This is faster and safer than writing complex exclusion rules.
Can I cancel an export while it is running?
Yes. You can tap \"Cancel\" in the dialog, or simply dismiss the dialog. The export runs safely in the background and you can return to check its progress at any time.
Is my code uploaded to a server?
Absolutely not. The plugin does not require internet permission. All scanning, filtering, and generation happens 100% locally on your device.
Where are the generated files saved?
Exported files are saved to your device\'s public storage under Download/OneCodeForAI.

Whitelist of extensions and glob patterns, evaluated before .gitignore.

Supported syntax (same as .gitignore patterns):
- Extensions: kt, json, xml
- Wildcards: *.log, src/*.kt
- Directories: build/

Any file matching an inclusion is exported even if .gitignore or exclusions would skip it.

Inclusions take priority over exclusions and over .gitignore. Use it to force-include specific files or extensions.

Unchecking the Inclusions box disables the list without deleting it: the rules stay in the profile and are reapplied the next time you check the box. The Clear button next to Add empties the list in one tap.

Blacklist of extensions and glob patterns.

Supported syntax (same as .gitignore patterns):
- Extensions: log, tmp, pyc
- Wildcards: *.log, src/*.bak
- Directories: build/

Any file matching an exclusion is skipped, even if .gitignore would include it. Inclusions take priority over exclusions.

To exclude a specific folder without writing a pattern, use the file tree below.

Unchecking the Exclusions box disables the list without deleting it: the rules stay in the profile and are reapplied the next time you check the box. The Clear button next to Add empties the list in one tap.

Patterns for files that should be listed in the dump but whose content is not read. Useful for lockfiles, generated code, and local configuration.

A reference-only file appears in the directory tree with a [ref] suffix and a size marker, but no content. The AI model learns that the file exists and how large it is, without receiving its body.

Supported syntax (same as inclusions and exclusions):
- Filenames: package-lock.json, local.properties
- Wildcards: *.lock

Reference-only patterns take priority over inclusions and exclusions. Inclusions take priority over exclusions.

Unchecking the Reference only box disables the list without deleting it: the patterns stay in the profile and are reapplied the next time you check the box. The Clear button next to Add empties the list in one tap.

Rules detected in the project's .gitignore file.

This list is read-only - edit .gitignore directly to change it.

Inclusions, exclusions, and reference-only patterns take priority over these rules: adding a matching rule forces the file in, out, or into reference-only mode regardless of .gitignore. Overridden rules are highlighted in amber. Negated rules (starting with '!') are shown with a distinct background so they can be told apart from positive rules.

Unchecking the Gitignore box disables the .gitignore rules without deleting the file: the rules stay on disk and are reapplied the next time you check the box.

Binary files are detected by a fixed list of known binary extensions (images, video, audio, archives, compiled binaries, fonts, databases). Files with these extensions are skipped so the dump stays focused on readable source code.

Detection is extension-based only. To skip an uncommon binary format, add its extension to Exclusions. To force-include one, add it to Inclusions, or to list it as reference-only, add it to Reference only.

Disabling this toggle includes the listed extensions in the export, which is rarely useful for AI context.

Shows the project tree with every entry the filters have selected. Each entry has three states:

- Included: the file's full content is written to the dump.
- Reference only: the file's name, size, and [ref] marker are written, but the content is not read.
- Excluded: the file is not written to the dump.

Click a row to cycle through the three states. Click a folder to apply the next state to its entire subtree, preserving the folder and its children in the same state.

Hard-excluded folders (like .git, node_modules) and binary files are initially locked: they are visible but disabled. Enable "Show locked" to unlock them and interact with them. Expanding an unlocked folder scans its contents on demand and shows every child, including the ones the rules would exclude, so you can navigate to build outputs and similar folders the initial scan skips.

Unchecking the File tree box hides the tree without losing your manual overrides: the selection is preserved and reapplied the next time you check the box.

Locked nodes are hard-excluded folders (like .git, node_modules, build) and binary files. They appear in the tree but cannot be interacted with until you enable "Show locked".

Why locked: these entries are excluded by default to keep the tree fast and to avoid accidentally dumping the contents of dependency folders. Enabling "Show locked" unlocks them so you can include, stub, or exclude them explicitly.

Locking is per-session. It is not saved to the project, because unlocking node_modules is almost always a one-off action.

When enabled, files larger than the selected size are skipped. This protects the dump from a single huge file (e.g. a bundled asset or generated SQL) dominating the output.

When disabled, every text file is included regardless of size, which can produce very large dumps. Combine it with the total export size limit in Settings to keep exports bounded.

Unchecking the Maximum size box does not delete the current value: the number stays in the field and is reapplied the next time you check the box.
